title: Multi-Chromium Interference Stack
scientific_hypothesis: Multiple thin Cr layers positioned at interference maxima within a HfO2/SiO2 stack will achieve broadband visible absorption through additive absorption across layers while dielectric spacing maintains high near-infrared reflectance.
design_principle: Distributing absorption across multiple thin metal layers positioned at standing wave maxima can broaden the absorption band compared to a single thick layer. Each Cr layer contributes absorption while dielectric layers between them maintain interference conditions for IR reflection. L26 supports metal/dielectric multilayer wavelength selectivity.
proposed_topology: Air / HfO2 / Cr / SiO2 / HfO2 / Cr / SiO2 / HfO2 / Cr / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / Al substrate
soft_objectives: Maximize broadband absorptance in 400-700 nm through multiple Cr layers
Balance Cr layer count with total layer budget
manufacturing_considerations: Total 13 layers including 3 Cr and 9 dielectric + Al substrate
Multiple Cr depositions increase process complexity
Each Cr layer must be thin enough to allow transmission to subsequent layers
theory_basis: Standing wave positioning for absorption enhancement
expected_advantages: Broader visible absorption band through multiple absorption events
Redundancy if one Cr layer underperforms
Flexible tuning through multiple thickness variables
known_risks: Multiple Cr layers may increase IR absorption
Process complexity higher than single-Cr designs
execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer stack with air incidence on an aluminum substrate. Stack sequence from air to substrate: HfO2 / Cr (Rakic-LD) / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / HfO2 / Cr (Rakic-LD) / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / HfO2 / Cr (Rakic-LD) / SiO2 (Lemarchand) / HfO2 / SiO2 (Lemarchand), terminating at aluminum substrate. Total layer count is 13 (3 Cr (Rakic-LD) + 10 dielectric + Al (Rakic-LD) substrate not counted as film layer). Optimize the thickness of each chromium layer independently and each dielectric layer thickness independently. Wavelength range 400-2000 nm. Target: maximize absorptance in 400-700 nm through distributed absorption, maximize reflectance in 700-2000 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light.
